articles.abstract: Metabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), have prompted interest in identifying natural products capable of modulating digestive enzymes. This study comparatively evaluated the phytochemical composition, antioxidant activity, and digestive enzyme inhibitory activities of green tea (GT), black tea (BT), and green coffee (GC) extracts. Phytochemical screening, antioxidant assays (DPPH, ABTS, and SOD-like), and quantitative phenolic analysis indicated that GT contained the highest phenolic content and exhibited the greatest antioxidant activity, whereas GC showed the highest alkaloid content. Among the fractionated extracts, the ethyl acetate fraction of green tea (EtOAc fraction of GT) was selected for further investigation based on its phenolic content, pancreatic lipase inhibitory activity, and overall biological profile. HPLC analysis identified ferulic acid and chlorogenic acid as major constituents, together with syringic acid, resveratrol, myricetin, and rosmarinic acid. Both the crude BT extract and EtOAc fraction of GT exhibited α-amylase inhibitory activity comparable to that of quercetin. articles.title: Nanoemulsions loaded with ß-caryophyllene and resveratrol for herpes infections.
articles.abstract: Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) infection represents a global health concern with a significant impact on affected individuals' quality of life. Conventional treatment relies on nucleoside analogues such as acyclovir, which, although effective, have limitations including viral resistance and low bioavailability. In this context, natural products such as resveratrol (RSV) and β-caryophyllene (BCP) emerge as promising alternatives due to their antiviral and immunomodulatory properties. However, these compounds present challenges related to stability and solubility, necessitating the use of controlled drug delivery systems such as nanoemulsions.

articles.title: Curcumin-loaded silk fibroin nanoparticle-stabilized pickering emulsions for co-delivery of resveratrol: Synergistic efficacy in strawberry preservation.
articles.abstract: Strawberries are nutrient-dense and economically vital fruits with extremely high perishability. They frequently suffer from postharvest losses and safety hazards due to their thin epidermis, active metabolism, and susceptibility to microbial infection. Conventional preservation strategies including refrigeration, chemical fungicides and polymer coatings suffer from chilling injury, health risks and high costs. Herein, we developed a novel Pickering emulsion stabilized by curcumin-loaded silk fibroin nanoparticles (Cur-SF NPs) for the co-delivery of resveratrol (Res) to synergistically enhance strawberry preservation. Formulated via a facile eco-friendly route, Cur-SF NPs serve as bifunctional stabilizers to enhance emulsion stability as well as solubility and stability of Res. Physicochemical characterization, antioxidant assays, and microbial tests verified the emulsion's favorable properties, revealing enhanced antioxidant activity and broad-spectrum antibacterial efficacy against Aspergillus niger and Escherichia coli. Integrated into chitosan edible coating, the emulsion effectively reduced strawberry weight loss, maintained firmness and inhibited spoilage. This green, sustainable strategy presents a highly viable approach for the postharvest preservation of soft fruits.

articles.title: A Review on Mechanisms of Action and Signaling Pathways of Natural Anti-hyperpigmentation Agents.
articles.abstract: Hyperpigmentation is a dermatological condition characterized by excessive melanin production, resulting in skin darkening. Intrinsic and extrinsic mediators, including ultraviolet (UV) radiation, hormonal changes, inflammation, and genetic predisposition, contribute to hyperpigmentation pathogenesis. The current review thoroughly examines the biological processes involved in hyperpigmentation, with particular emphasis on its signaling pathways, particularly the cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), wingless-related integration site (Wnt)/β-catenin, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt), and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), thereby providing mechanistic insights that may facilitate the development of effective treatments. The review also evaluates the safety, toxicity, and therapeutic efficacy of TYR inhibitors, arbutin, azelaic acid, ellagic acid, kojic acid, resveratrol, and the melanosome inhibitor niacinamide, for managing hyperpigmentation. Additionally, the review summarizes the in vitro and in vivo studies of these agents and other emerging plant extracts. Recent advances in the use of plant extracts for hyperpigmentation have shown promising efficacy; nevertheless, their translation into clinical and commercial applications remains limited. This limited translation might be attributed to the challenges related to standardization and the paucity of clinical evidence regarding long-term safety. Moreover, ongoing studies on natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents have highlighted the critical role of patent analyses in the advancement of biomedical research. This review provides a strategic direction for researchers to assess the safety, efficacy, and toxicity profiles of natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents.

articles.title: Phytopharmacological and Functional Insights Into the Bioactive Compounds of Grape (Vitis vinifera L.): An Integrated Review of In Vitro, In Vivo, and Clinical Studies.
articles.abstract: Grapes (Vitis vinifera L.) are abundant in polyphenols, flavonoids, and other bioactive constituents. They exhibit a wide range of health-promoting properties, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anticancer, cardioprotective, antidiabetic, and skin anti-aging effects. We review and summarize the phytopharmacological and functional effects of grape-derived compounds. This review includes in vitro, in vivo, and clinical studies. The search combined the terms "V. vinifera" OR "grape" with keywords related to traditional uses, phytochemistry, and pharmacological activities. Peer-reviewed English-language studies published between 2000 and 2025 reporting ethnobotanical uses, phytochemical composition, or pharmacological effects were included. The findings were synthesized qualitatively. This review showed that grape seed and red grape extracts inhibited the growth of MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells. articles.title: Development of sericin-elastin nanoblends containing resveratrol for cosmeceutical applications.
articles.abstract: Resveratrol (RSV), a high-value phytocompound upcycled from winemaking byproducts, is highly promising for cosmeceutical applications against oxidative stress due to its extraordinary antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties. However, its topical application is severely limited by chemical instability, poor aqueous solubility, and rapid degradation by light and oxygen. To overcome these limitations and maximize epidermal efficacy, a biocompatible nanoblend composed of sericin and elastin was developed. The sericin (4 mg/mL)/elastin (2 mg/mL) nanoblends showed an average diameter of 140 nm, a narrow size distribution, a Zeta potential of -35 mV and high stability at pH 7 and 10, as well as at temperatures between 32 °C and 37 °C. The encapsulation of RSV (0.4 mg/mL) did not affect the mean diameter and polydispersity index of the systems, allowing an entrapment efficiency of ∼30% (drug content of 0.12 mg/mL). The release profile showed a biphasic kinetic trend over time. When tested on HaCaT human keratinocytes, both single polymers and blend nanosystems demonstrated excellent tolerability, confirming the high biocompatibility of the formulation. Furthermore, RSV-loaded blend nanoparticles showed a superior cytoprotective effect compared to the free drug, a trend confirmed by DPPH, CellROX and MitoSOX assays. Finally, CompuSyn analysis validated a strong synergy between the carrier and RSV (CI < 1) with a synergistic effect at 10 µg/mL with a Dose Reduction Index (DRI) of 3.00. In conclusion, the developed sericin-elastin nanoblends containing RSV represent innovative cosmeceuticals characterized by strong antioxidant activity able to be employed for the topical treatment of skin disorders.
